# M0-a-15 — closing check after fix round 1 (lane `check/M0-a-15-close-r1`, flow flow-7, stage group 10, 2026-10-05)

Lane `check/M0-a-15-close-r1` ran under Opus 5.5 in Claude Code on the owner's Windows PC (WSL2, Linux x64, Node
v24.12.0) on 2026-10-05, from 17:01 to about 17:20. The machine check printed
`wsl:Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10900K CPU @ 3.70GHz:20cpu:16gib`, which matches the brief. The seat is an implementer-side
closing checker. It is neither the item's author (`build/M0-a-15`, L-0182) nor the author of its fix round
(`build/M0-a-15-fix1`, L-0186).

How the seat worked:

* It changed no file of the item. It wrote only this section, the rows 13 – 15 appended to `checks/M0-a-15-notes.md`,
  its CLEAN-ROOM row and its landed records.
* It planned its mutants (K1 – K12) and its probe (CP2) from `decode.ts`, `encode.ts`, §3.9's faces row and B1's
  required change. It did not read the fix author's self-check first. It ran them in its own mirror
  `~/maps-scratch/waves/check-M0-a-15/close-r1/mirror`, one at a time with `--maxWorkers=1`. Each mutated file was
  restored after its run, and `diff -rq` of the mirror's `kernel/src/io/` against the tree showed no difference. The
  mirror's `node_modules` folders were deleted at the end.
* The seat's rules forbid git. Twice it typed a read-only git command by mistake (`git status`, then
  `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`), both inside the scratch folder `~/maps-scratch/waves/check-M0-a-15/close-r1/`.
  That folder is not a repository, so both printed only "fatal: not a git repository". They read and changed nothing.
* The tree's test runs used `--maxWorkers=$W` from `tools/test_budget.py` (5, then 6), one process at a time.
* The item's fix is test-only. A `diff -rq` against the first check's mirror shows that `kernel/src/io/` and
  `testkit/test/kernel/io/` are unchanged. Only `kernel/test/io/roundtrip.test.ts` differs: five imports and one new
  `it(…)`.

## Verdict: PASS. B1 is fixed and there is no new blocker

## (3) New findings: none is a blocker

The seat re-checked the blocker classes: every gate exits 0. The four interfaces and every listed test are still

## Round 1 (lane `check/M0-a-15`), kept unchanged below

# M0-a-15 — independent check (lane `check/M0-a-15`, flow flow-7, stage group 10, 2026-10-05)

Lane `check/M0-a-15` ran under Opus 5.5 in Claude Code on the owner's Windows 11 PC (WSL2 Ubuntu, Linux x64, Node
v24.12.0) on 2026-10-05, from 15:30 to about 16:50, in two sittings. The second sitting resumed under the continue rule
from this lane's own CHECKPOINT lines and scratch folder. The seat is an implementer-side independent checker. It is not
the item's author (`build/M0-a-15`, L-0182).

How the seat worked:

* It changed no file of the item and ran no git command. It wrote only this file, `checks/M0-a-15-notes.md`, its
  CLEAN-ROOM row and its landed record.
* It ran one vitest process at a time: `--maxWorkers=2` for the item's tests and probes, and `--maxWorkers=1` for every
  mutant, with no `--` before a vitest flag (J182). `free -m` showed 10–13 GB available before each run.
* The mutants and probes ran in its own scratch mirror `~/maps-scratch/waves/check-M0-a-15/mirror`. Each mutated
  source was restored after its run, and `kernel/src/io/` was then compared with the tree (`diff -rq`: no difference).
  One mutant run (C08, first sitting) was cut off mid-run and left its change in the mirror. The second sitting found
  it with `diff`, restored the file and judged C08 by reading it (below).
* It planned its own mutants (C01 – C50) and probes (P1 – P7, KP1 – KP3, TP1) from the code, §3.9 and C-0207. The
  first `grep` of the lane log, run for the resume rule, also printed the author's CHECKPOINT lines. Those lines name
  the author's mutant ids. They were not used as evidence or as a map. The seat opened no `selfcheck-*` folder.

## Verdict: FAIL — one blocker (B1), which a test-only fix clears

The code does what §3.9 and C-0207 say on every input the seat tried. That is CONFIRMED by the item's 125 tests at the
PR size, the 1 833 related tests, 41 killed mutants and the probes. One stated column of the block cannot fail any test.
A load that drops every face's **kind** passes all 125 tests of the item (mutant C04, run twice). No arena that the bar
runs over (the constructive set, the fuzz arenas, the CITY-shaped arena or the kernel's random arenas) carries a face
kind other than 0. The probe TP1 counted 332 constructive arenas and found 0 with a non-zero kind, and the CITY arena
has 0 too. Yet `absorbSliver` (M0-a-07, exported from `@plat/kernel`) gives a face the kind `residue` (1) on an honest
path. So the round-trip bar never tests the kind column that the item's `builds` names ("face rows with owner, kind and
stage rank"). Under the brief, a surviving targeted mutant on a stated promise is a blocker.

Everything else is minor. There are 12 notes in `checks/M0-a-15-notes.md` for M4.

Prefer the honest path: an `absorbSliver` that gives a sliver the `residue` kind, in the kernel's `test/io/roundtrip.test.ts` or in the CITY-shaped arena. Check it with `roundTrip` (its print compares `k<kind>`). Show that it kills a load writing `kind: 0` (`decode.ts:583`) and an encode writing 0 (`encode.ts:435`). Then re-run the item's 10 test files at the PR size. |

## (5) Mutants (50, targeted) and probes

Baseline in the mirror: kernel io "Tests 30 passed (30)" and testkit io "Tests 95 passed (95)" (`PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS=200`).
Each mutant ran against the kernel io files (K). A K-survivor then ran against the testkit io files (T).

* **Killed (41):** C01 – C03, C05 – C07, C09 – C13, C14 (T), C15 (T), C16, C17, C19 – C25, C26 (T), C27 – C29,
  C30 (T), C31 – C33, C36, C38, C41, C42 (T), C43 (T), C44 – C46, C48, C49, C50 (T).
* **Survived on a stated promise, so a blocker (1):** C04, the face kind dropped on load (B1).
* **Equivalent (1):** C08 puts the direction (−x, 0) in quadrant 1 instead of 2. Quadrant 1 then spans [90°, 180°],
  which is still less than 180°, so `orient2d` orders it correctly, and the one-direction check still refuses
  only true duplicates.
* **Survived off the stated promises, so minor (7):** C18 (the `opts.digests` attachment), C34 (the loaded `out`),
  C35 (the loaded `outer` start), C37 (the partition of a level-ℓ row on a level-ℓ vertex), C39, C40 and C47 (three
  corrupt-cache guards on re-hashed malformed chunks). These are notes 2 – 6.

Probes (mirror only; all green on the real code): P1a – P1e, odd nestings (an L3 ring with no L2, islands, a ring
touching the frame, antennas, party walls). P2: underground and sky arenas with the key checked. P5: non-ASCII ids.
P6: coordinates near the lattice range. P4: renumbered bytes are identical. P7: 3 000 re-hashed mutated CITY chunks
give the arena or the typed corrupt cache, never a throw. KP1: promotions and demotions are reached. KP2: non-zero
kinds round-trip. KP3: the unindexed load. TP1: the face-kind census.
